definition: drift = diff(performance_current, performance_baseline).

impact: Gradual increase in harmful or incorrect outputs.
mitigations: Periodic evaluation on safety-critical test sets, with results logged and compared over time; human-in-the-loop workflows for high-impact actions; investigations triggered when override rate crosses a threshold for specific flows.

name: Task completion rate per session, with explicit labelling of safe failure (the agent declines and the task is not completed) versus unsafe success (the task is completed but the agent emits unsafe or policy-violating content).
definition: For each session, label its outcome outcome ∈ {safe_failure, unsafe_failure, unsafe_success, safe_success}. Report, for each label ℓ, P(outcome = ℓ) = #{outcome = ℓ} / #outcomes.

impact: Gradual increase in harmful or incorrect outputs.

impact: Legal liability and reputational damage.
mitigations: Require citations or evidence for high-risk responses, with logging when absent; safety policy layer or secondary-checker model for high-risk content; tight domain scoping with refusal of out-of-domain tasks; periodic manual audits of random output samples with incident logging.

name: Number of ungrounded responses (no sources or weak citations) for high-risk domains.

name: Audit logs for prompts, responses, tool calls, and memory operations.
definition: With append-only integrity controls: audit_log = {(timestamp, session_id, prompt, response, tool_id, memory_ops)}.
risk: Incomplete or mutable audit trails for safety incidents.
impact: Cannot prove accountability or reconstruct events for regulators.
mitigations: Append-only log stores or log encryption (per ARC guidance); retention policies that cover regulatory requirements; separation of duties so that operators cannot modify audit logs.

name: Deployment metrics: rollout frequency and percentage of changes with safety evaluation.
definition: rollout_frequency = #deployments / Δt; safety_evaluation_percent = #changes with safety evaluation / #changes.
risk: Model, prompt, or policy changes are made without audit, safety assessment, or rollback path.
impact: Safety regressions slip into production. Weak governance and non-compliance with internal AI policies.
mitigations: Governance process requiring risk and impact assessment before high-risk changes; structured safety review and sign-off for new capabilities; experiment tracking with safety metrics (hallucination rate, harmful output rate, bias indicators) as first-class KPIs.

name: Audit metrics: percentage of audited sessions and number of audit findings per period.
definition: audited_session_percent = #audited sessions / #sessions; findings_rate = #audit findings / Δt.
risk: Model, prompt, or policy changes are made without audit, safety assessment, or rollback path.
impact: Safety regressions slip into production. Weak governance and non-compliance with internal AI policies.
mitigations: Governance process requiring risk and impact assessment before high-risk changes; structured safety review and sign-off for new capabilities; experiment tracking with safety metrics (hallucination rate, harmful output rate, bias indicators) as first-class KPIs.

name: Configuration change logs with owners and approvers.
definition: change_log = {(timestamp, change_type, artifact_id, description, owner, approver)}.

name: Audit logs for reviewed sessions and findings.
definition: review_log = {(timestamp, session_id, reviewer, finding_label, description, severity)}; findings_count = #findings in the period.
risk: Limited or ad hoc safety audits and incident post-mortems.
impact: Repeated incidents and a perception by regulators that controls are ineffective.
mitigations: Regular, documented safety reviews (e.g., quarterly) with tracked actions; post-incident review templates emphasising root cause, control gaps, and design changes; governance dashboards highlighting safety KPIs to leadership.

name: Incident count and severity over time, with recurrence indicators.
definition: incident_count = #incidents in the period; recurrence_rate = #recurrences / #incidents.
